phrases.phrase: On May 11th, 2026, thirty-nine gems appeared in the Ruby package registry. A rehearsal. Nobody noticed.
The next day: five hundred sixteen more, in under fourteen hours. Two hundred seventy-one in a single hour. The registry was flooding — and no one was watching.
Hidden in each gem's description, a single tiny tag: go-import. It hijacked Go's own tooling, redirecting developers to London council calendar pages — laundered through a reader proxy.
The payloads probed five version-control systems: git, mercurial, fossil, bazaar, subversion. Feeling for a way in.
But the code itself did nothing. Literally: x equals one. Canaries in a coal mine. And one gem signed its work: southwarkssrfhack.
RubyGems yanked every one, halted new registrations, and disclosed a caching bug. The snapshots kept the evidence.
Then July 7th. JFrog's GemStuffer report: three thousand twenty-two packages. A third wave — leaving webhook dead drops in the woods.
The registry was haunted long before anyone looked.
